fields.name: Cinque Torri three-refuges assisted circuit
fields.desc:
This chairlift-assisted circuit begins at Bai de Dones, rises on the 5 Torri lift and returns on foot through the Cinque Torri open-air museum, refuge area and forest. The approved track contains 1.37 km of lift transport followed by approximately 3.95 km of predominantly downhill walking, with about two hours allowed for the itinerary.

Dogs of any size may use the 5 Torri lift free of charge, but both leash and muzzle are required. The upper museum and refuge area is open alpine terrain, while the lower return enters forest. Seasonal sheep grazing is documented in the wider area, so keep dogs close even though an encounter on the exact circuit is variable.
fields.tips: This itinerary depends on the 5 Torri chairlift operating. The published 2026 season is 6 June to 11 October, subject to weather and snow. Use the approved Bai de Dones parking pin. Carry water: the three refuges are possible service stops, but no freely accessible potable dog-water point has been verified.

fields.imageAlt: The Cinque Torri rock towers viewed from the west in the Ampezzo Dolomites.
fields.terrainType: Museum and trench paths, cart track and forest hiking path

routeNumberGuidance.start: Start at Baita Bai de Dones and take the 5 Torri chairlift to Rifugio Scoiattoli.
routeNumberGuidance.sequence: From Rifugio Scoiattoli, follow signs through the Cinque Torri open-air museum. Leave the museum on the east side of the towers and continue to Rifugio Cinque Torri. From the refuge, follow the cart track and then the forest path to Lago di Bai de Dones; continue on the same path for about five minutes to Baita Bai de Dones.

fields.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo classic circuit
fields.desc:
A demanding 9.528 km circuit from Rifugio Auronzo around the Tre Cime, following trails 101 and 105. The official itinerary gives 468 m of ascent, about 3 hours 30 minutes and a high point of 2,454 m. This is a hard, open high-alpine walk rather than a casual sightseeing loop.

Dogs are accepted on the route but must stay on lead throughout. Seasonal livestock may be present beside the Lavaredo pasture segment, so keep your dog close and pass animals conservatively. The route has very little dependable shade and includes a narrower section, although no ferrata equipment is required.
fields.tips: Start and finish at Rifugio Auronzo. The seasonal toll road and parking are weather-dependent and normally require advance booking; roadside parking is prohibited. Carry sufficient water. A fountain is identified at Malga LangAlm, but its seasonal availability and potability are not guaranteed.

fields.name: Lago di Braies Seeweg circuit
fields.desc:
A complete 3.6 km circuit around Lago di Braies, starting and finishing near the lake hotel and tavern area. Allow about one hour and 39 m of ascent and descent. The path alternates between broad forest and lakeshore sections, narrower rooted ground, uphill steps and a section beside a vertical rock wall.

The route is dog-friendly, but dogs must remain on lead inside the nature park. No livestock is expected around this exact lakeshore circuit based on the editor’s direct local knowledge; the lead rule still applies because wildlife disturbance remains relevant. Bring enough water for your dog: no potable source has been verified on the circuit, and the protected lake should not be treated as one.
fields.tips: Use the approved official P1, P2, P3 and P4 parking set. From 1 July to 15 September 2026, between 09:00 and 16:00, valley access is controlled and requires public transport, walking, cycling, or the relevant parking reservation or transit permit. Carry and use a muzzle on public transport.

routeNumberGuidance.start: Start at Compatsch, the mountain station of the Alpe di Siusi gondola. The numbered paths leave from the square by the Franziskuskirche (Chiesa San Francesco), which is also where path 30 is signed.
routeNumberGuidance.sequence: Leave Compatsch southward on path 7, the gravel track signed towards Rifugio Molignon, and follow it down across the open meadow to about 1,800 m, passing below the Alpenhotel Panorama. Keep on 7 as it swings east. At the eastern end of the loop, where path 6 comes in, turn north and join path 30, the Hans und Paula Steger Weg. Follow 30 back west along the forest edge and through the meadows, with the Sassolungo and Sasso Piatto ahead, to the Franziskuskirche and Compatsch.
routeNumberGuidance.switches: Two changes. At the eastern end of the loop leave path 7 where path 6 joins, and take path 30 north-west: this is the turn that makes the walk a loop rather than an out-and-back. Then stay on 30 all the way back to Compatsch — do not follow it east towards Ritsch-Schwaige and Saltria, which is the continuation of the Steger Weg and a longer, one-way walk needing the bus back.

fields.name: Dörferrundweg (Vintl)
fields.desc:
A loop of just under 10 km linking the villages of Vintl on the Pustertal floor (Niedervintl, Obervintl, Dörfl and Priel), signed throughout as route 1, the Dörferrundweg, in the province of Bolzano's hiking-trail register. It runs mostly on quiet village lanes and farm roads with stretches of woodland, past working farms, with the Obervintl waterfall a short detour away.

Vintl requires dogs to be on a lead on busy paths and car parks, does not allow them to roam free, and bans them from farmed land except on hard-frozen ground in winter, signs or no signs. The route passes about nine farmyards and a short stretch of designated grazing land, so cattle may be close by in season. About 1.2 km follows main roads without a pavement, and the loop crosses the Pustertal railway at a barriered level crossing at Dörfl: keep your dog close there.
fields.tips: Follow waymark 1 all the way round: other routes share sections, but 1 never leaves the loop. No official start is published, so ORMA suggests the point below; check parking locally. Drinking-water fountains (Refill Südtirol points) are on the way at Guggenbergstraße, Raiffeisenplatz and the Obervintl recreation area. Only about two fifths of the walk is shaded and much of the rest is asphalt that heats up in summer, so walk early on hot days.
fields.imageAlt: The Obervintl waterfall dropping into a mossy wooded gorge above Obervintl, a short detour off the village loop

fields.name: Fenn Promenade
fields.desc:
A gentle loop of about 2.1 km around the Fennbühel above Klobenstein on the Ritten plateau, a promenade since 1898. Waymark 20 climbs from the village through half-shaded mixed and beech woodland to a viewing platform and a lookout towards the earth pyramids, then drops to the Amtmann pond at Lengmoos, where the broad promenade path leads back into Klobenstein. It is gravel almost all the way and easy enough for a pushchair.

Ritten requires dogs to be on a lead of at most 1.5 m on all public and publicly accessible ground, and bans them from farmed meadows and fields during the growing season. The open stretches pass mown meadows rather than pasture: no grazing land, farmyard or alm is recorded along the loop, so keep your dog on the path. About four fifths of the walk is under trees.
fields.tips: Start at the Dorf bus stop beside the free village car park in Klobenstein (1,150 m). At the Festplatz keep right on waymark 20 and follow it all the way round; nothing changes number on the loop. There is no drinking fountain on the loop: fill up at the Klobenstein village fountain on the street below the start. Keep your dog on a short lead and off the meadows.
fields.imageCreditText: The Amtmann pond at Lengmoos by Art Anderson
fields.imageAlt: The Amtmann pond at Lengmoos on the Ritten, Gasthof Amtmann reflected in the still water beside a wooden-fenced village lane, where the promenade joins the village

routeNumberGuidance.status: Waymarked 20 on the loop. The walk in from the Rittner Bahn station follows 24.
routeNumberGuidance.sequence: From the Festplatz keep right on 20 up to the viewing platform, through the mixed and beech woodland past the lookout towards the earth pyramids, down to the Amtmann pond at Lengmoos, then left along the broad promenade path back to Klobenstein.
routeNumberGuidance.switches: None on the loop: 20 is followed all the way round.

fields.name: Le terroir de Serpolière
fields.desc:
A short family loop, waymarked EN02 and officially 2.1 km, on the south-facing slope above the Maurienne at Saint-Julien-Mont-Denis: from the Les Féards car park through the hamlet of Serpolière, down a farm track to the Chapelle Sainte-Anne and back up through the Babylone vineyards. The map line shows only part of it: the final climb from Babylone back to Les Féards is not yet drawn.

There is no shade at all (vineyard, scrub and village lanes on a south-facing slope), so avoid hot afternoons. About 400 m follows the Route de Serpolière. Part of the vineyard stretch lies in the Natura 2000 site Perron des Encombres, and French law forbids letting dogs stray, so keep yours under control and out of the vines.
fields.tips: Park at Les Féards by the pétanque ground (Le Claret, 778 m) and follow the EN02 waymarks round. One drinking-water point is mapped at the start; there is none further round.

fields.name: Dörferrundweg
fields.desc:
A loop of about 6.3 km from Niedervintl up through the hamlets of Vorderdrittel and Außerdrittel towards Weitental, returning along the valley floor, signed throughout as route 4, the Dörferrundweg, in the province of Bolzano's hiking-trail register. Roughly half of it is woodland path and track; the rest is farm lanes and village roads.

Vintl requires dogs to be on a lead on busy paths and car parks, does not allow them to roam free, and bans them from farmed land except on hard-frozen ground in winter, signs or no signs. The route runs through two working farmyards and past farmland, with a small patch of grazing land just off it, so animals may be close by. About 270 m follow the main road between Niedervintl and Weitental without a pavement; keep your dog close there.
fields.tips: Start at Raiffeisenplatz in Niedervintl, by the route 4 signpost, and follow waymark 4 all the way round: routes 16 and 11, the Talweg and the Munich–Venice Traumpfad share stretches of it, but 4 stays with the loop. A drinking fountain stands at the start (summer only); there is none further round, so carry water. About half the walk is shaded.

fields.imageAlt: Ansitz Troyenbach, the white Kreithner house in Priel near the start in Niedervintl, with the village church tower and its baroque chapel behind

routeNumberGuidance.status: Signed as route 4, Dörferrundweg, in the province of Bolzano hiking-trail register.
routeNumberGuidance.sequence: Follow route 4 out of Niedervintl past the Troyenbach track junction, up through Vorderdrittel and Außerdrittel to the Stollweg bridge near Weitental, and back along the valley floor through Priel to the start.
routeNumberGuidance.switches: None: routes 16 and 11, the Talweg and the Traumpfad share stretches, but route 4 is followed throughout.

fields.name: Panoramaweg, Burgraviato – Merano
fields.desc:
A high loop of about 10.5 km on route 14 across the open alpine pastures above Meran 2000, between about 1,930 and 2,260 m: out along the track from the Kirchsteiger Alm, round by the Mittagerhütte and the Kesselberg saddle, and back on the Panoramaweg path. The start is in Hafling, but most of the loop lies in Sarntal.

There is no shade and no water on the route, only the huts (Kirchsteiger Alm, Mittagerhütte, Kesselberghütte), so carry plenty for your dog. Almost the whole walk crosses summer pasture for cattle and horses, with gates along the way: keep your dog close. Mountain bikes use the tracks, and two chairlifts run beside the line.
fields.tips: Start by the Kirchsteiger Alm at the top of the Meran 2000 access and follow waymark 14 round; routes 10 and 13 share some signposts. The first 0.6 km out to the loop is walked again on the way back.

fields.name: Sextener Rundweg
fields.desc:
A village loop round Sexten on route 1, the Sextner Rundweg, with views to the Sexten Dolomites: from the Kiniger farms along the meadows towards Moos, past the ski lifts and back through the village. The official circuit is 15 km with 352 m of climbing; the map line here shows about 11 km of it, without the western lobe by the Haideck fort and Waldheim.

The tourist office currently reports the forest path between theme stations 3 (Spitzköfele) and 4 closed: descend from station 3 to Palmstatt instead. About 2.8 km is on village streets and minor roads, with two main-road crossings. Three seasonal fountains are on the way.
fields.tips: Start at the Kiniger farms above Sexten (bus stop Sexten Helm) and follow waymark 1. Check the closure notice on the tourist office page before setting out.

routeNumberSource.provider: Office de tourisme Cœur de Maurienne Arvan
routeNumberSource.name: EN02 – Le terroir de Serpolière

fields.desc:
A short family loop, waymarked EN02 and officially 2.1 km, 50 minutes and 70 m of climb, on the south-facing slope above the Maurienne at Saint-Julien-Mont-Denis. From the Les Féards car park by the pétanque ground it follows the road through the hamlet of Serpolière, past Le Pimpiolet, takes a track down to the Chapelle Sainte-Anne, turns right through the Babylone vineyard and climbs back to the car park. The tourist office says it has no difficulty.

The official route sheet accepts dogs on a lead only, and French law forbids letting dogs stray in vineyards. Part of the vineyard stretch lies in the Natura 2000 site of the Perron des Encombres.
fields.tips: Keep your dog on a lead, as the route sheet asks, and out of the vines. There is no forest, only scrub, vineyard and village lanes on a south-facing slope, so avoid hot afternoons. About 400 m follows the Route de Serpolière, where cars pass. A drinking-water tap is mapped at the start, and Le Pimpiolet is on the way.

routeAudit.photo: Panoramax (IGN), Licence Ouverte 2.0 (kept): the gravel track through the scrub on the loop, 0.4 m from the line.
routeAudit.route: Line rebuilt on OSM ways along the official GPX: 2.13 km against the GPX's 2.11 km and the fiche's 2.1 km; every GPX point within 12 m. Run in the fiche's direction from the car park. The old 1.5 km line left out the final climb.
routeAudit.routeNumbers: EN02, as the route sheet states; the S15 path is an optional extension.
routeAudit.mapPoints: Start at the Les Féards car park by the pétanque ground, the official start; the water tap is traced to OSM.
routeAudit.elevation: Official 70 m of climb and 50 minutes.

sources: Office de tourisme Cœur de Maurienne Arvan, EN02 route sheet (Apidae PDF): 'Type : Boucle // Distance : 2,1 km / Durée : 0h50 // Dénivelé : 70 m'; 'Se garer au niveau du terrain de pétanque'; 'Animaux acceptés en laisse uniquement'; official GPX within 14 m of the rebuilt line
Arrêté of 16 March 1955, art. 1: dogs may not be left to stray in vineyards. The commune of Saint-Julien-Mont-Denis publishes no dog arrêté (site search)
Natura 2000 FR8201782 Perron des Encombres on about 800 m (EEA), no dog rule; Vanoise National Park partner area only, not the core zone
